video.description:
Learn to explain how SwiftUI custom layouts measure and place their views: ProposedViewSize, LayoutSubviews & Layout Protocol, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ProposedViewSize - The size a parent suggests to a view, which the view can accept or ignore.
LayoutSubviews - The collection of child views that a custom layout measures and places.
Layout Protocol - A protocol for a custom container that measures its children and places them.

landscape.hook: Can you explain ProposedViewSize, LayoutSubviews and Layout Protocol in English?

dialogue.title: A custom tag layout

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, HStack cannot wrap my tags to a new line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then write a custom layout with the Layout Protocol.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does the Layout Protocol need?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two steps. It measures its children, and then it places them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How big can each child be?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The parent sends a ProposedViewSize, like `width: 100`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does the child have to use that size?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, it can accept or ignore the ProposedViewSize.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And where are the children inside my layout?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They come as LayoutSubviews. You loop over them to measure and place each one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I tried to place the tags before I measured them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Measure first with the LayoutSubviews, then place them. The Layout Protocol follows that order.
A parent sends a ProposedViewSize to its child.
